old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a steam locomotive in motion, with thick plumes of white smoke billowing from its engine. The camera focuses on the intricate details of the locomotive's wheels, which are painted red and black, and the mechanical components beneath them. As the train moves forward, the smoke continues to rise, partially obscuring the view of the locomotive's body. The background is blurred due to the speed of the train and the dense smoke, but hints of industrial structures can be seen in the distance. The overall atmosphere is one of historical and mechanical power, evoking a sense of nostalgia for the era of steam-powered transportation. The camera remains steady throughout, emphasizing the locomotive's movement and the dynamic interplay between the train and the surrounding environment.

caption: The video captures a close side view of a steam locomotive's driving-wheel gear, red spoked wheels with bright steel rims joined by horizontal coupling rods beneath a black boiler. A thin red valve rod runs along the running-board line while a heavy steam cloud billows around the wheelset, a steel gantry at upper left at the start. The wheels turn continuously, the crank pins sweeping their circular cycle so the long rod to the crosshead tilts and re-levels repeatedly, marking steady motion. The framing tightens on the lower mechanism, the gantry sliding out of view and the boiler edge lifting toward the top of frame. A dense steam mass builds on the right, progressively hiding the front wheel, cylinder and valve gear. The rear wheels stay visible through the haze, still rotating as the locomotive shifts leftward within the crop.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
